events.text: Salvador Dalí paints The Persistence of Memory, with its melting watches
Edward Hopper paints Nighthawks, his late-night diner scene
Van Gogh paints The Starry Night from his asylum window at Saint-Rémy
Rembrandt completes The Night Watch in Amsterdam

reveal.explanation: Rembrandt's great militia portrait belongs to the Dutch Golden Age, nearly two and a half centuries before Van Gogh painted his swirling night sky in 1889. Dalí's melting watches and Hopper's lonely diner are closer together than they may feel, with the surrealist dreamscape of 1931 arriving eleven years before the American realist's best-known picture.

sources.excerpt: The Night Watch was completed in 1642 at the peak of the Dutch Golden Age.
Painted in June 1889, it depicts the view from the east-facing window of his asylum room at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, just before sunrise, with the addition of an imaginary village.

The Persistence of Memory (Catalan: La persistència de la memòria, Spanish: La persistencia de la memoria) is a 1931 painting by artist Salvador Dalí and one of the most recognizable works of Surrealism.
Nighthawks is a 1942 oil on canvas painting by the American artist Edward Hopper that portrays four people in a downtown diner late at night, as viewed through the diner's large glass window.
